# Reference: Third-Party Hosted Access for DeepSeek V4

Where to consume DeepSeek V4 (Pro and Flash) without sending traffic to DeepSeek's PRC-hosted API. Pricing, jurisdiction, context-window caveats, and provider-quality variance as of 2026-04-27 (Day-3 post-launch).

DeepSeek V4 was released 2026-04-24 [1]. The model weights are open and available for self-hosting; multiple Western inference providers brought hosted endpoints up within 72 hours. The headline numbers below are list pricing — production performance and quality vary materially between providers (see "Provider variance" below).

## Provider pricing — V4-Pro and V4-Flash side by side

All figures USD per 1M tokens.

| Provider | V4-Pro input | V4-Pro output | V4-Pro cached | V4-Flash input | V4-Flash output | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **DeepSeek direct (standard, post-2026-05-05)** | $1.74 | $3.48 | $0.0145 | $0.14 | $0.28 | [2] |
| **DeepSeek direct (promo until 2026-05-05 15:59 UTC)** | $0.435 | $0.87 | $0.003625 | $0.14 | $0.28 | [2] |
| **OpenRouter** | $0.435 | $0.87 | not specified | $0.14 | $0.28 | [3][4] |
| **Together AI** | $2.10 | $4.40 | $0.20 | not published | not published | [5] |
| **DeepInfra** | $1.74 | $3.48 | $0.145 | not published in this fetch | not published in this fetch | [6] |
| **NVIDIA NIM (build.nvidia.com)** | "free during developer preview" — no per-token figure published | — | — | — | — | [7] |

Key arithmetic, against DeepSeek direct pricing:

- **OpenRouter** matches DeepSeek's promotional rate ($0.435 / $0.87) for V4-Pro [3] and DeepSeek's standard Flash rate exactly ($0.14 / $0.28) [4]. Effective premium over DeepSeek direct: **0%** (during promo); will become **-75%** (i.e., the same rate, but DeepSeek direct will be more expensive once promo ends 2026-05-05 unless OpenRouter raises).
- **DeepInfra** matches DeepSeek's *standard* (post-promo) rate exactly on input/output: $1.74 / $3.48 [6]. **However, DeepInfra charges $0.145/1M for cached input — 10× DeepSeek's $0.0145/1M cache-hit rate.** For cache-heavy workloads (long shared system prompts, agent loops with stable context), the parity claim erodes substantially. Premium over DeepSeek standard: **0% on input/output, +900% on cache hits**. Premium over DeepSeek's current promo rate: **+300% on input/output**.
- **Together AI** charges $2.10 / $4.40, a **+21%** input markup and **+26%** output markup versus DeepSeek standard, and **+383% / +406%** versus DeepSeek's current promo [5].
- **NVIDIA NIM** lists hosted endpoints on build.nvidia.com without published per-token pricing during developer preview [7]. Treat as "evaluation only" until pricing is posted.

## Context window — meaningful divergence between providers

DeepSeek advertises 1M tokens for both V4-Pro and V4-Flash [1][2].

| Provider | Stated context window | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek direct | 1M tokens | Both Pro and Flash [2] |
| OpenRouter | 1,048,576 tokens (1M) | Both Pro and Flash [3][4] |
| Together AI | **512K tokens** | **Half the advertised window** — Together appears to cap context at 512K [5] |
| DeepInfra | 1M tokens (full context honored) | Page also notes 65,536 tokens as "standard operations max context" [6] — meaning unclear; possibly default-vs-extended request mode. Confirm before relying on long-context calls. |
| NVIDIA NIM | not specified in this fetch | [7] |

**Practical implication:** Together AI is the wrong provider for any workflow that depends on the full 1M window (large monorepos, long-document agents). If long-context fidelity matters, route to DeepSeek direct, OpenRouter, or DeepInfra.

## Jurisdiction

| Provider | Hosting jurisdiction | Compliance posture |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek direct | **PRC** | DeepSeek operates from China; standard CN-jurisdiction data exposure assumptions apply [1][2] |
| OpenRouter | US | Routes to provider pool that *may include DeepSeek itself* — provider routing is the user's responsibility to constrain [3] |
| Together AI | US (San Francisco) | Data terms / data residency / rate limits not disclosed on the V4-Pro product page [5] |
| DeepInfra | not specified | **SOC 2 Certified, ISO 27001 Certified** [6]; data residency details not on this page |
| NVIDIA (build.nvidia.com) | US | NVIDIA Developer Program endpoints [7] |

OpenRouter is a **routing layer**, not a single jurisdiction. Its pool can include DeepSeek's own endpoint as a downstream provider, which negates the "Western host" premise. To enforce jurisdiction on OpenRouter, the caller must use provider preferences / allowlists at the API level — that configuration is not in scope of the fetched product pages.

## Provider variance and quality (this is the load-bearing finding)

OpenRouter's October 2025 Exacto announcement is the canonical evidence that **identical model weights produce different tool-calling behavior across providers** [8]. Key quotes and findings, applied to DeepSeek V3.1 (the announcement predates V4 but establishes the pattern):

- "Significant variance in both tool-calling accuracy and propensity between providers hosting identical models" [8].
- Three measured failure modes: **invalid JSON returns, incorrect tool names, schema mismatches** [8].
- DeepSeek 3.1 specifically showed a "tight band of performance" across providers, with Deepinfra remaining competitive **even as the sole provider using fp4 quantization** [8].
- "Performance gaps tend to narrow as providers optimize inference stacks post-launch" [8].

Two practical consequences for V4 specifically:

1. **Quantization disclosure varies.** DeepInfra publicly states FP4 + FP8 mixed (MoE in FP4, the rest in FP8) [6]. Together AI does not disclose precision on its V4-Pro product page [5]. NVIDIA's blog cites MXFP4 as the native model format [7]. Together's silence is a documented gap, not a confirmed quality issue — but it makes apples-to-apples comparison impossible without independent benchmarks.
2. **OpenRouter's Exacto endpoints** route to providers meeting three criteria: top tool-calling accuracy, normal propensity ranges, and low user-blacklist rates [8]. As of the fetched announcement, Exacto launched with five models including DeepSeek v3.1 Terminus; **a V4 Exacto endpoint is not confirmed in the fetched material** — flag as a gap.

## Jurisdictional escape from PRC data exposure

For buyers whose concern with the DeepSeek API is Chinese-jurisdiction data routing rather than the model weights themselves, the open-weights release [1] enables a **clean separation**: the model can be served from a Western-jurisdiction host without traffic touching PRC infrastructure. The cost premium for that separation is bounded:

- **DeepInfra**: 0% premium over DeepSeek's standard rate, with SOC 2 + ISO 27001 [6].
- **Together AI**: +21% input / +26% output over DeepSeek standard, jurisdiction US [5], but at 512K context only [5].
- **OpenRouter**: 0% premium during the promo window, but provider pool may include DeepSeek itself unless constrained [3][4].

This is the practical mitigation pattern for individual and small-team buyers who want V4-class capability without sending prompts to CN-hosted infrastructure.

## Recommendation by buyer profile

- **Privacy-sensitive (must avoid PRC routing, want a compliance posture):** DeepInfra. 0% premium over DeepSeek standard, US-hosted, SOC 2 + ISO 27001 [6]. Caveat: data residency specifics not on the product page; verify before any regulated workload.
- **Cost-sensitive (price is the primary axis):** OpenRouter at promo pricing matches DeepSeek direct exactly [3][4]. Constrain provider routing to exclude DeepSeek's own endpoint if jurisdiction matters.
- **Production reliability (predictable throughput, willing to pay for it):** Together AI [5] or DeepInfra [6]. Together's 21-26% markup buys a single-vendor SLA story; DeepInfra's 0% premium plus stated certifications is the better economic case unless Together's throughput numbers (not published in fetched material) win on independent benchmarks.
- **Day-3 caveat applies to everyone:** "Performance gaps tend to narrow as providers optimize inference stacks post-launch" [8]. Provider quality on Day 3 is not the steady-state quality at Day 30+. Avoid hard-coding a provider into production agent stacks until the post-launch optimization curve flattens. Plan to re-benchmark in 2-4 weeks.
